message.content: What is NVIDIA's platform strategy?|NVIDIA's platform strategy involves bringing together hardware, software, algorithms, libraries, systems, and services to create unique value for the markets they serve, using a unified underlying architecture that leverages their GPUs and software stacks.|NVIDIA has a platform strategy, bringing together hardware, software, algorithms, libraries, systems, and services to create unique value for the markets we serve. While the requirements of these end markets are diverse, we address them with a unified underlying architecture leveraging our GPUs and software stacks.

What are the capabilities of NVIDIA's GPUs that support deep learning algorithms?|NVIDIA's GPUs have parallel processing capabilities supported by up to thousands of computing cores, which are essential for running deep learning algorithms.|Its parallel processing capabilities, supported by up to thousands of computing cores, are essential to running deep learning algorithms.

How much has NVIDIA invested in research and development since its inception?|NVIDIA has invested over $24 billion in research and development since its inception.|Innovation is at our core. We have invested over $24 billion in research and development since our inception, yielding inventions that are essential to modern computing.

What fields have NVIDIA's GPU architecture expanded into beyond PC graphics?|NVIDIA has expanded into scientific computing, artificial intelligence, data science, autonomous vehicles, robotics, and augmented and virtual reality.|Since our original focus on PC graphics, we have expanded to several other large and important computationally intensive fields, including scientific computing, artificial intelligence, or AI, data science, autonomous vehicles, or AV, robotics, and augmented and virtual reality, or AR and VR.

How did NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 impact modern computer graphics?|NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 defined modern computer graphics and established NVIDIA as the leader in visual computing.|Our invention of the GPU in 1999 defined modern computer graphics and established NVIDIA as the leader in visual computing.

What are some of the applications powered by NVIDIA's GPU-powered deep learning?|GPU-powered deep learning is adopted for applications such as accelerating molecular dynamics simulations, weather forecasting, and powering AI in enterprises for services and products that would be impossible with traditional coding.|GPU-powered deep learning is being adopted by thousands of enterprises to deliver services and products that would have been impossible with traditional coding. Researchers use our GPUs to accelerate a wide range of important applications, from simulating molecular dynamics to weather forecasting.

What percentage of supercomputers on the global TOP500 list are powered by NVIDIA GPUs?|NVIDIA powers nearly 70% of supercomputers on the global TOP500 list, including 8 of the top 10.|Including GPUs and networking, NVIDIA powers nearly 70%, and 8 of the top 10, supercomputers on the global TOP500 list.

What was the value of the transaction for NVIDIA to acquire Arm from SoftBank?|$40 billion|NVIDIA entered into an agreement with Arm Limited and SoftBank to acquire all allotted and issued ordinary shares of Arm in a transaction valued at $40 billion.
How much cash did NVIDIA pay at the signing of the acquisition agreement with SoftBank?|$2 billion|NVIDIA paid $2 billion in cash at the signing of the Share Purchase Agreement with SoftBank.

What could SoftBank receive if Arm achieves certain financial performance targets by March 31, 2022?|SoftBank could receive either up to an additional $5 billion in cash or up to an additional 10.3 million shares of NVIDIA common stock.|The transaction includes a potential earn-out, which is contingent on the achievement of certain financial performance targets by Arm during the fiscal year ending March 31, 2022. If achieved, SoftBank can elect to receive either up to an additional $5 billion in cash or up to an additional 10.3 million shares of NVIDIA common stock.

What are the main components of NVIDIA's Graphics segment?|GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs, GeForce NOW game streaming service, Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs, vGPU software, and automotive platforms for infotainment systems.|NVIDIA's Graphics segment includes GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs, the GeForce NOW game streaming service, Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs, vGPU software for cloud-based visual and virtual computing, and automotive platforms for infotainment systems.

In which four large markets does NVIDIA specialize that require tremendous application acceleration?|Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive markets|NVIDIA's platforms address four large markets where their expertise is critical: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive.

What technology does NVIDIA's RTX line-up feature for real-time, cinematic-quality rendering in games?|Ray tracing technology|The NVIDIA RTX line-up features ray tracing technology for real-time, cinematic-quality rendering, which simulates the physical behavior of light to achieve greater realism in computer-generated scenes.

What happens if the Purchase Agreement between NVIDIA and Softbank is terminated under certain circumstances?|NVIDIA will be refunded $1.25 billion of the Signing Consideration.|If the Purchase Agreement is terminated under certain circumstances, NVIDIA will be refunded $1.25 billion of the Signing Consideration.

What industries benefit from NVIDIA's Professional Visualization platforms?|Design and manufacturing, digital content creation, automotive, media and entertainment, architectural engineering, oil and gas, and medical imaging.|Our Professional Visualization platforms are critical enablers in many fields, such as design and manufacturing and digital content creation. Design and manufacturing encompass computer-aided design, architectural design, consumer-products manufacturing, medical instrumentation, and aerospace. Digital content creation includes professional video editing and post-production, special effects for films, and broadcast-television graphics.

What is the NVIDIA RTX platform used for?|Rendering film-quality, photorealistic objects and environments with physically accurate shadows, reflections, and refractions using ray tracing in real-time.|The NVIDIA RTX platform makes it possible to render film-quality, photorealistic objects and environments with physically accurate shadows, reflections and refractions using ray tracing in real-time.

Which companies are NVIDIA's partners in bringing AI to enterprise users?|IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, and VMware.|We partnered with industry leaders such as IBM, Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, and VMware to bring AI to enterprise users.

What purpose do NVIDIA's GPUs serve in the AI field?|They excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.|At the foundation of the NVIDIA accelerated computing platform are our GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads such as the training and inferencing of neural networks.

What are some applications that utilize NVIDIA's virtual reality technology?|Virtual car showrooms, surgical training, architectural walkthroughs, and bringing historical scenes to life.|Just as VR is becoming more important in gaming, it is also being incorporated in a growing number of enterprise applications. Virtual car showrooms, surgical training, architectural walkthroughs, and bringing historical scenes to life all deploy this technology, powered by our GPUs.

What acquisition did NVIDIA complete in fiscal year 2021?|NVIDIA completed the acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, Ltd.|In fiscal year 2021, we completed the acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, Ltd., or Mellanox, a supplier of high-performance interconnect and networking products that are now part of our Data Center market platform.

[Irrelevant]Which major cloud service providers offer NVIDIA's GPUs?|Alicloud, Amazon Web Services, Baidu Cloud, Google Cloud, IBM Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud.|They are available in industry standard servers from every major computer maker worldwide, including Cisco, Dell, HP, Inspur, and Lenovo; from every major cloud service provider such as Alicloud, Amazon Web Services, Baidu Cloud, Google Cloud, IBM Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud.

Who did NVIDIA acquire in fiscal year 2021 to enhance its Data Center market platform?|Mellanox Technologies, Ltd.|In fiscal year 2021, we completed the acquisition of Mellanox Technologies, Ltd., a supplier of high-performance interconnect and networking products that are now part of our Data Center market platform.

What new class of processor did NVIDIA announce that is supported by the DOCA architecture?|Data processing unit (DPU)|We announced a new class of processor – the data processing unit, or DPU – supported by a novel data-center-infrastructure-on-a-chip architecture, or DOCA, that enables breakthrough networking, storage and security performance.

What software products does NVIDIA offer to support powerful GPU performance for virtual machines?|NVIDIA virtual GPU (vGPU) software products|NVIDIA vGPU software products enable powerful GPU performance for workloads ranging from graphics-rich virtual desktops and workstations to data science and AI. Installed on a physical GPU in a cloud or enterprise data center server, NVIDIA vGPU software creates virtual GPUs that can be shared across multiple virtual machines accessed on any device, anywhere.

Which cloud partners does NVIDIA collaborate with for deploying AI and HPC applications?|Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud|AI developers, researchers and data scientists can deploy their applications on DGX systems, NGC-ready workstations or servers from NVIDIA systems partners, or with NVIDIA’s cloud partners such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, or Oracle Cloud.

DRIVE AutoPilot|Our Xavier system-on-a-chip, or SoC, which started shipping in 2018, enables vehicles to use deep neural networks to process data from multiple cameras and sensors. It powers the DRIVE AutoPilot, NVIDIA’s Level 2+ automated driving solution, combining the DRIVE AV self-driving solution with the DRIVE IX cockpit software.

What simulation solution does NVIDIA offer for testing self-driving platforms before deployment?|NVIDIA DRIVE Constellation running DRIVE Sim software|We offer a scalable data center-based simulation solution, NVIDIA DRIVE Constellation running DRIVE Sim software, for testing and validating a self-driving platform before commercial deployment.

What does NVIDIA’s DRIVE platform use to perceive and understand in real-time around the vehicle?|Deep learning, sensor fusion, and surround vision|NVIDIA DRIVE can perceive and understand in real-time what is happening around the vehicle, precisely locate itself on an HD map, and plan a safe path forward. This advanced self-driving car platform combines deep learning, sensor fusion, and surround vision to change the driving experience.

What is the primary approach mentioned for addressing complex issues in the transportation industry due to autonomous driving?|A top-to-bottom and end-to-end approach.|A top-to-bottom and end-to-bottom approach will enable the transportation industry to solve the complex problems arising from the shift to autonomous driving.

How does the company make its intellectual property available to customers and partners?|Through license and development agreements.|Our intellectual property is a valuable asset that can be accessed by our customers and partners through license and development agreements when they desire to build such capabilities directly into their own products, or have us do so through a custom development.

What is a key aspect of the company's worldwide sales and marketing strategy?|Collaborating with end customers and industry ecosystems through a partner network.|Our worldwide sales and marketing strategy is key to achieving our objective of providing markets with our high-performance and efficient computing platforms. Our sales and marketing teams, located across our global markets, work closely with end customers and various industry ecosystems through our partner network.

Who are part of the company's partner network in their sales strategy?|Industry's OEMs, ODMs, system builders, AIBs, retailers/distributors, internet and cloud service providers, automotive manufacturers and suppliers, mapping companies, start-ups, and other ecosystem participants.|Our partner network incorporates each industry's respective OEMs, original device manufacturers, or ODMs, system builders, add-in board manufacturers, or AIBs, retailers/distributors, internet and cloud service providers, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, mapping companies, start-ups, and other ecosystem participants.

What type of manufacturing strategy does the company use for its semiconductors?|A fabless manufacturing strategy.|We do not directly manufacture semiconductors used for our products. Instead, we utilize a fabless manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ world-class suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.

Which suppliers does the company use for semiconductor wafer production?|Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd.|We utilize industry-leading suppliers, such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd, to produce our semiconductor wafers.

What does the company's Deep Learning Institute offer to developers?|In-person and online training to build AI and accelerated computing applications using their platforms.|Our Deep Learning Institute provides in-person and online training for developers in industries and organizations around the world to build AI and accelerated computing applications that leverage our platforms.

From which companies do we purchase substrates and memory for our semiconductor products?|Substrates are purchased from Ibiden Co. Ltd., Kinsus Interconnect Technology Corporation, and Unimicron Technology Corporation. Memory is sourced from Micron Technology, Samsung Semiconductor, Inc., and SK Hynix.|We purchase substrates from Ibiden Co. Ltd., Kinsus Interconnect Technology Corporation, and Unimicron Technology Corporation, and memory from Micron Technology, Samsung Semiconductor, Inc., and SK Hynix.

Where do we ship semiconductor products after performing quality assurance and configuration?|Semiconductor products are shipped to contract equipment manufacturers (CEMs), distributors, motherboard and add-in card (AIC) customers from our third-party warehouse in Hong Kong, Israel, and the United States.|We typically receive semiconductor products from our subcontractors, perform incoming quality assurance and configuration, and then ship the semiconductors to contract equipment manufacturers, or CEMs, distributors, motherboard and add-in card, or AIC, customers from our third-party warehouse in Hong Kong, Israel, and the United States.

Who are some of the contract manufacturers (CMs) and original design manufacturers (ODMs) we utilize for product manufacturing?|We utilize contract manufacturers such as Flex Ltd. and Fabrinet, and original design manufacturers such as Wistron Corporation.|We also utilize industry-leading contract manufacturers, or CMs, such as Flex Ltd. and Fabrinet, and ODMs such as Wistron Corporation, to manufacture some of our products for sale directly to end customers.

What are considered principal competitive factors in our market?|Principal competitive factors in our market include performance, breadth of product offerings, access to customers and partners, distribution channels, software support, conformity to industry standard APIs, manufacturing capabilities, processor pricing, and total system costs.|We believe that the principal competitive factors in this market are performance, breadth of product offerings, access to customers and partners and distribution channels, software support, conformity to industry standard APIs, manufacturing capabilities, processor pricing, and total system costs.

Who are some of our current competitors in the market?|Current competitors include suppliers and licensors designing discrete and integrated GPUs and HPC solutions like AMD, Intel, and Xilinx; large internet services companies like Alphabet Inc. and Amazon, Inc.; SoC product suppliers like Ambarella, Inc., Broadcom Inc., and Qualcomm; and suppliers of interconnect solutions like Applied Optoelectronics, Cisco Systems, and Arista Networks.|Our current competitors include: suppliers and licensors designing discrete and integrated GPUs and other accelerated computing solutions, including chipsets that incorporate 3D graphics, or HPC, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, Intel Corporation, and Xilinx, Inc.; large internet services companies with internal teams designing chips that incorporates HPC or accelerated computing functionality as part of their internal solutions or platforms, such as Alphabet Inc. and Amazon, Inc.; suppliers of SoC products that are embedded into automobiles, autonomous machines, and gaming devices, such as Ambarella, Inc., AMD, Broadcom Inc., Intel, Qualcomm Incorporated, Renesas Electronics Corporation, Samsung, and Xilinx or companies with internal teams designing SoC products for internal use, such as Tesla Motors; and suppliers of interconnect, switch and cable solutions such as Applied Optoelectronics, Inc., Arista Networks, Broadcom, Cisco Systems, Inc., Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company, Intel, Juniper Networks, Inc., Lumentum Holdings, Marvell Technology Group, and Xilinx, as well as internal teams of system vendors and large internet services companies such as Alphabet and Amazon.

What measures do we rely on to protect our intellectual property in the United States and internationally?|We rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, employee and third-party nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect our intellectual property.|We rely primarily on a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets, employee and third-party nondisclosure agreements, and licensing arrangements to protect our intellectual property in the United States and internationally.

What are some factors considered when deciding whether to seek formal protection for innovations and technologies?|Factors include the location in which products are manufactured, strategic technology or product directions in different countries, and the degree to which intellectual property laws exist and are enforced in different jurisdictions.|We continuously assess whether and where to seek formal protection for particular innovations and technologies based on such factors as: the location in which our products are manufactured; our strategic technology or product directions in different countries; the degree to which intellectual property laws exist and are meaningfully enforced in different jurisdictions; and

What factors influence the decision to seek formal protection for innovations and technologies in certain locations?|The decision to seek formal protection for innovations and technologies is influenced by factors such as the location of product manufacturing, strategic technology or product directions in different countries, the degree of enforcement of intellectual property laws, and the commercial significance of operations in specific countries and regions.|We continuously assess whether and where to seek formal protection for particular innovations and technologies based on such factors as: the location in which our products are manufactured; our strategic technology or product directions in different countries; the degree to which intellectual property laws exist and are meaningfully enforced in different jurisdictions; and the commercial significance of our operations and our competitors' operations in particular countries and regions.

How does the company describe its compliance with worldwide governmental regulations in relation to capital expenditures and operations?|The company states that compliance with various laws, rules, and regulations has not materially affected their capital expenditures, results of operations, or competitive position.|Our worldwide business activities are subject to various laws, rules, and regulations of the United States as well as of foreign governments. Compliance with these laws, rules, and regulations has not had a material effect upon our capital expenditures, results of operations, or competitive position.

What percentage of new hires came from internal recommendations, as noted in the recruitment overview?|Over 36% of hires came from internal recommendations.|We partner with higher education institutions globally to develop our candidate pipelines, recruit at industry conferences, and encourage our employees to submit referrals, with over 36% of hires coming from internal recommendations.

What methods does the company use to evaluate employee sentiment and engagement?|The company uses pulse surveys, a suggestion box, and an anonymous third-party hotline to evaluate employee sentiment and engagement.|To evaluate employee sentiment and engagement, we use several listening mechanisms such as pulse surveys, a suggestion box, and an anonymous third-party hotline.

What roles were created to enhance diversity and inclusion efforts in fiscal year 2021?|In fiscal year 2021, the company created the role of Head of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging, along with hiring a global diversity recruiting leader.|We have increased our efforts to recruit, develop, and retain a more diverse workforce with a focus on those historically underrepresented in the technology field. In fiscal year 2021, we created the role of Head of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging, along with hiring a global diversity recruiting leader.
What is the company’s stated turnover rate for fiscal year 2021?|The turnover rate for fiscal year 2021 was 3.8%.|In fiscal year 2021, our overall turnover rate was 3.8%.

Why does the company provide equity to employees, according to the compensation, benefits, and well-being section?|The company provides equity to employees to encourage them to invest in the company’s future and align their interests with those of the stockholders, as it is tied to the value of the company's stock price and vests over time.|Our compensation program rewards performance and is structured to encourage employees to invest in the company’s future. Employees receive equity that is tied to the value of our stock price and vests over time to retain employees while simultaneously aligning their interests with those of our stockholders.

What new position was created to support diversity efforts in fiscal year 2021?|Head of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging|In fiscal year 2021, we created the role of Head of Diversity, Inclusion, and Belonging, along with hiring a global diversity recruiting leader, and a Head of Strategic Initiatives to build our developer ecosystem and ensure it represents the global population.
What percentage of the company's global workforce was male as of January 31, 2021?|80%|As of January 31, 2021, our global workforce was 80% male and 20% female.

Who is the President and Chief Executive Officer of the company?|Jen-Hsun Huang|Jen-Hsun Huang is the President and Chief Executive Officer. Jen-Hsun Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and has served as our President, Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Board of Directors since our inception.
What role does Colette M. Kress hold at NVIDIA?|Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer|Colette M. Kress is the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA.

What measures were taken to protect employees during the COVID-19 pandemic?|Implemented global protocols including office closures, remote work resources, safety protocols for essential workers.|We implemented global protocols to slow the spread of COVID-19 by closing our offices around the world for all except essential workers, eliminated most business travel, provided resources for remote work, instituted safety protocols for essential labs and offices.

What degrees does Jen-Hsun Huang hold?|B.S.E.E. degree from Oregon State University and an M.S.E.E. degree from Stanford University.|Mr. Huang holds a B.S.E.E. degree from Oregon State University and an M.S.E.E. degree from Stanford University.

Which demographic groups are the focus of the company's diversity recruitment efforts?|Women, Black, and Hispanic candidates.|We have increased our efforts to recruit, develop, and retain a more diverse workforce with a focus on those historically underrepresented in the technology field, including women, Black, and Hispanic candidates.

What positions did Debora Shoquist hold at NVIDIA?|Senior Vice President of Operations in 2007 and Executive Vice President of Operations in 2009.|Debora Shoquist joined NVIDIA in 2007 as Senior Vice President of Operations and in 2009 became Executive Vice President of Operations.
Where did Mr. Puri receive his M.B.A. degree?|Harvard Business School.|Mr. Puri holds an M.B.A. degree from Harvard Business School.
What type of company is Coherent, Inc.?|A manufacturer of commercial and scientific laser equipment.|Coherent, Inc. is a manufacturer of commercial and scientific laser equipment.

What degrees does Mr. Teter hold?|A B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of California at Davis and a J.D. degree from Stanford Law School.|Mr. Teter holds a B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of California at Davis and a J.D. degree from Stanford Law School.

[Irrelevant] From which universities did Ms. Shoquist earn her degrees?|Kansas State University (B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering) and Santa Clara University (B.S. degree in Biology).|Ms. Shoquist holds a B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering from Kansas State University and a B.S. degree in Biology from Santa Clara University.

What roles did Timothy S. Teter hold at NVIDIA, and in what years?|Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary in 2017, and became Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary in February 2018.|Timothy S. Teter joined NVIDIA in 2017 as Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary and became Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary in February 2018.

What kind of information can be found on the SEC's website?|Reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers that electronically file with the SEC.|The SEC’s website contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC.

What are the four large markets addressed by NVIDIA's GPU-based visual and accelerated computing platforms?|Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive|Our GPU-based visual and accelerated computing platforms address four large markets: Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive. These markets often experience rapid technological change, changes in customer requirements, new product introductions and enhancements, and evolving industry standards.

Why is it important for NVIDIA to win product design opportunities in markets where they do not sell directly to consumers?|Winning product design opportunities is crucial because it involves anticipating customer demands, and failure to secure these design wins may prevent NVIDIA from obtaining future opportunities, which could lead to lost revenue and weaken its competitive position.|For our products that we do not sell directly to consumers, achieving design wins is an important success factor, including for our interconnect products. Achieving design wins may involve a lengthy process in pursuit of a customer opportunity and depend on our ability to anticipate features and functionality that customers and consumers will demand. Failure to obtain a particular design win may prevent us from obtaining design wins in subsequent generations of a particular product. This could result in lost revenue and could weaken our position in future competitive bid selection processes.

What are some activities NVIDIA must engage in to meet the evolving needs of its markets?|NVIDIA must engage in identifying emerging industry changes, developing new products, enhancing existing products, and making technical, financial, compliance, sales, and marketing investments.|Our success depends on our ability to identify emerging industry changes and to develop new (or enhance our existing) products, services and technologies that meet the evolving needs of these markets. Such activities may require considerable technical, financial, compliance, sales and marketing investments.

What could happen if NVIDIA fails to develop new products or focus on widely adopted technologies?|Failure to develop new products or focus on technologies that become widely adopted could adversely affect NVIDIA's business, revenue, financial condition, and results of operations.|Additionally, we continue to make considerable investments in research and development, which may not produce significant revenue for several years, if at all. If our investments are unsuccessful and we fail to develop new products, services and technologies, or if we focus on technologies that do not become widely adopted, our business, revenue, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.

NVIDIA needs to evolve to manage the social and environmental impact of its products, expand the ecosystem for its products, and monetize and expand its business to prevent negative financial impacts.|If we do not continue to evolve our business, including by developing market specific technologies, managing the social and environmental impact of our products and technologies, expanding the ecosystem for our current and future products and technologies, and monetizing and expanding our business in various areas, our financial results could be negatively impacted.

What challenges might NVIDIA face if its products are not in compliance with industry standards?|If NVIDIA's products are not in compliance with industry standards, customers may not incorporate the products into their design strategies, potentially leading to lost sales and incompatibility with major hardware and software.|Unanticipated changes in industry standards could render our products incompatible with products developed by major hardware manufacturers and software developers. Additionally, if our products are not in compliance with prevailing industry standards, including safety standards, our customers may not incorporate our products into their design strategies.

How might the competitive landscape impact NVIDIA's revenue growth?|The competitive landscape could hinder NVIDIA's revenue growth as competitors may offer less costly products with superior functionality, potentially resulting in lower selling prices for NVIDIA's products and challenges in identifying and capitalizing on new market opportunities.|Competition in our current and target markets could prevent us from growing our revenue. Our target markets remain extremely competitive, and we expect competition to intensify as current competitors expand their product and/or service offerings, industry standards continue to evolve, customer needs change and new competitors enter these markets. Our competitors’ products, services and technologies may be less costly, or may offer superior functionality or better features, than ours, which may result, among other things, in lower than expected selling prices for our products. In addition, some of our competitors operate and maintain their own fabrication facilities, have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, and greater financial, sales, marketing and distribution resources than we do. These competitors may be able to more effectively identify and capitalize upon opportunities in new markets and end user customer trends, quickly transition their products.

Why might the company experience lower than expected selling prices for its products?|Competitors may offer superior functionality or better features, potentially resulting in lower expected selling prices for the company's products.|offer superior functionality or better features, than ours, which may result, among other things, in lower than expected selling prices for our products.

What are some of the advantages that competitors may have over the company?|Competitors may have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios, and greater resources in finances, sales, marketing, and distribution.|some of our competitors operate and maintain their own fabrication facilities, have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, and greater financial, sales, marketing and distribution resources than we do.

What risks are associated with the company's dependency on third-party foundries for manufacturing?|Risks include lack of guaranteed supply of wafers, potential higher wafer costs, failure to secure adequate manufacturing capacity, and low manufacturing yields.|We depend on third parties and their technology to manufacture, assemble, test and/or package our products... we face several significant risks...a lack of guaranteed supply of wafers... higher wafer and component prices...a failure by our foundries to provide or allocate adequate manufacturing...low manufacturing yields.

What might happen if the company fails to successfully compete in its target markets?|Failing to compete may result in decreased demand for its products, services, and technologies, causing its revenue to decline and operations to suffer.|If we are unable to successfully compete in our target markets, respond to changes in our target markets or introduce new offerings...demand for our products, services and technologies could decrease, which would cause our revenue to decline and cause our results of operations to suffer.

How could consolidation in target markets affect the company?|Consolidation could lead to fewer customers, partners, or suppliers, negatively affecting the company's financial results.|the competitive landscape in our target markets has changed and may continue to evolve due to a trend toward consolidation, which could lead to fewer customers, partners, or suppliers, any of which could negatively affect our financial results.

What impact could low manufacturing yields have on the company?|Low manufacturing yields could harm customer relationships, increase manufacturing costs, and negatively impact business operations, gross margin, and revenue.|In addition, low manufacturing yields could have an adverse effect on our ability to meet customer demand, increase manufacturing costs, harm customer or partner relationships, and/or negatively impact our business operations, gross margin, revenue and/or financial results.

What challenges does the company face regarding product design and manufacturing yield improvements?|Challenges include dependency on process technology which is typically proprietary to the foundry and lack of knowledge about potential yield problems until the design is manufactured.|Manufacturing yields for our products are a function of product design, which is developed largely by us, and process technology, which typically is proprietary to the foundry. Low yields may result from either product design or process technology failure. We do not know whether a yield problem will exist until our design is actually manufactured by the foundry.

What are the main factors that influence the yields of products?|Product yields are influenced by product design and process technology, which is typically proprietary to the foundry.|Products are a function of product design, which is developed largely by us, and process technology, which typically is proprietary to the foundry. Low yields may result from either product design or process technology failure.

Why might yield problems not be identified until well into the manufacturing process?|Yield problems may not be identified until well into the manufacturing process because it is unknown if a yield problem will exist until the design is actually manufactured by the foundry.|We do not know whether a yield problem will exist until our design is actually manufactured by the foundry. As a result, yield problems may not be identified until well into the manufacturing process and require us and the foundry to cooperate to resolve the problem.

What causes delays in the introduction of new products or product enhancements?|Delays in the introduction of new products or product enhancements can be caused by the inability of available software development tools to fully simulate the complex features and functionalities of products.|In the past, we have experienced delays in the introduction of products and enhancements as a result of the inability of then available software development tools to fully simulate the complex features and functionalities of our products.

What are the potential consequences of products containing significant defects?|If products contain significant defects, it can lead to substantial remediation expenses, damage to reputation, loss of market share, and increased warranty, support, and repair costs.|If our products contain significant defects, we could incur significant expenses to remediate such defects, our reputation could be damaged, and we could lose market share. Our products, including both hardware and software offerings, are complex and may contain defects or security vulnerabilities, or experience failures or unsatisfactory performance due to any number of issues in design, fabrication, packaging, materials and/or use within a system.

How could product errors affect consumer perceptions?|Product errors could harm relationships with customers and partners, harm consumers’ perceptions of the brand, and result in failure to achieve market acceptance or loss of design wins.|An error or defect in new products or releases or related software drivers after commencement of commercial shipments could result in failure to achieve market acceptance or loss of design wins, harm our relationships with customers and partners and harm consumers’ perceptions of our brand.

What risks are associated with inaccurate estimation of customer demand?|Inaccurate estimation of customer demand could lead to a mismatch between supply and demand, resulting in product shortages or excess inventory and negatively impacting financial results.|If we fail to estimate customer demand properly, our financial results could be harmed. Our products are manufactured based on estimates of customers’ future demand and our manufacturing lead times are very long. This could lead to a significant mismatch between supply and demand, giving rise to product shortages or excess inventory.

What could happen if there is a failure to achieve design wins for products?|Failure to achieve design wins for products could harm the business, potentially leading to a decline in market share and reduced revenues.|If we fail to achieve design wins for our products, our business will be harmed.

What are some potential causes for excess or obsolete inventory in a company?|Potential causes for excess or obsolete inventory include changes in business and economic conditions, a decrease in demand for products, rapidly changing technology, introduction of new products, less demand than expected for newly introduced products, and increased competition.|Situations that may result in excess or obsolete inventory include: changes in business and economic conditions, including downturns in our target markets and/or overall economy; changes in consumer confidence caused by changes in market conditions, including changes in the credit market; a sudden and significant decrease in demand for our products; a higher incidence of inventory obsolescence because of rapidly changing technology or customer requirements; our introduction of new products resulting in lower demand for older products; less demand than expected for newly-introduced products; or increased competition, including competitive pricing actions.

How could volatility in the cryptocurrency market impact the demand for gaming GPUs?|Volatility in the cryptocurrency market, including changes in cryptocurrency prices, can impact demand for gaming GPUs as these are capable of digital currency mining. Changes to cryptocurrency standards and processes like Ethereum 2.0 can also affect demand.|Demand for our products is based on many factors, including our product introductions and transitions, competitor announcements, and competing technologies, all of which can impact the timing and amount of our revenue. For example, our GPUs for gaming are capable of digital currency mining. Demand and use of GPUs for cryptocurrency has fluctuated in the past and is likely to continue to change quickly.
